name: a shallow rain puddle lying on the ground, reflecting a pale sky band, with a soft damp earth halo and only a faint low bank shadow along its far edge
label: wasteland_ruins/puddle

surfaces.part: puddle water ellipse with pale sky reflection streaks
damp earth ground tile with halo

answer.evidence: The sprite is a full 64x48 earth ground tile, with every row 64 px wide. A small teal puddle sits in the middle, rows 20-28. Its width profile widens and narrows again, so it is an ellipse seen from above. It has dark blue shading along its far (top) edge and light blue reflection streaks at rows 24-26. There is no vertical front face, no front-edge line and no eave shadow, so this is a flat decal with no south face. That is the expected look for a flat object, and it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a brown soil patch with mottled light and dark clumps and a small blue puddle with a paler reflection band. The soil ramp has about 4 steps and the puddle about 3, against roughly 5-6 steps in the grass and paving references, so it is a little shallower in steps. The measured facts do not show it as shallow. It has 5 visible tones per tile, between the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 2%, so there are no large flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the edges carry a brown tint rather than a black sticker line. The total of 9 raw colours is modest, but the soil grain and the damp halo keep the surface varied and consistent with the references. A careful artist would accept it next to them, though it is slightly sparser and less detailed than the grass.
